newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev/mark up to 996, lev/dlr off to 1,843.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev/mark up to 996, lev/dlr off to 1,843.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 996 per mark on Monday, up from 996-998 at the opening and 996-997 at Friday's close as mark demand eased in the afternoon following earlier interest-rate linked buying, traders said.
* The lev fell to 998-999 per mark at midday as foreign currency demand rose because local banks built up positions to profit from higher foreign currency interbank deposit rates, dealers said.
* Interbank overnight lev depo rates stood at 1.50-1.75 percent annually against three percent on overnight mark deposits.
* Foreign exchange buying from final customers also pressured the lev in early trade.
* The lev closed at 1,840-1,843 to the dollar, down from the morning's 1,837-1,841 and in line with a fall in mark/dollar on global markets.

* The lev has been pegged at 1,000 per mark, the anchor currency in an IMF-prescribed fixed-exchange rate mechanism known as currency board. The currency board system was introduced on July 1 to restore confidence in the lev.

* Under the currency board system, Bulgaria's central bank pledged to buy and sell unlimited volumes of the mark, or anchor currency, at a fixed bid of 995 levs and ask of 1,000. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
